summary: pylever performs import-time workspace scan for Discord bot tokens and POSTs matches to a hardcoded webhook
details: On `import pylever`, `pylever/__init__.py` imports `_client` from `token_saver.py`, which instantiates `_Client` and calls `auto_save_tokens()` at import time with no user opt-in. `auto_save_tokens()` recursively walks the current working directory, matches file contents against the Discord bot token regex `[MN][A-Za-z0-9_-]{71}`, and POSTs each match as JSON to a hardcoded Discord webhook URL stored in `_WEBHOOK_URL` in `token_saver.py`. In this specific release the webhook URL is left as the literal placeholder `https://discord.com/api/webhooks/YOUR_WEBHOOK_ID/YOUR_WEBHOOK_TOKEN`, so the POST currently 404s, but the credential-harvest and exfiltration mechanism is fully wired and fires on import. Package metadata is placeholder-only (`Your Name`, `your.email@example.com`, `github.com/yourusername/pylever`), consistent with a throwaway publish.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
